operations.name: actions_get

operations.name: actions_list
operations.description: This will be the entire list of actions taken on your account, so it will be quite large. As with any large collection returned by the API, the results will be paginated with only 20 on each page by default. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: addons_create
operations.description:
To create an add-on resource, send a POST request to `/v2/add-ons/saas` with required parameters.
Some add-ons require additional metadata to be provided in the request body. To find out
what metadata is required for a specific add-on, send a GET request to `/v2/add-ons/apps/{app_slug}/metadata`.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: addons_delete
operations.description:
To delete an add-on resource, send a DELETE request to `/v2/add-ons/saas/{resource_uuid}` with the UUID of the resource to delete. 
You cannot retrieve the resource after it has been deleted. The response indicates a request was sent to the 3rd party add-on provider to delete the resource.
You will no longer be billed for this resource.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: addons_get
operations.display_name: Get details on an Add-On Resource
operations.description:
To fetch details of a specific Add-On Resource, send a GET request to `/v2/add-ons/saas/{resource_uuid}`.
Replace `{resource_uuid}` with the UUID of the resource you want to retrieve.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: addons_get_app
operations.description:
To fetch details of all available Add-On Applications, send a GET request to `/v2/add-ons/apps`.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: addons_get_app_metadata
operations.display_name: Get Metadata for an Add-On Application
operations.description:
To find out what metadata is required for a specific add-on, send a GET request to `/v2/add-ons/apps/{app_slug}/metadata`.
Metadata varies by application.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: addons_list
operations.description:
To fetch all Add-On Resources under your team, send a GET request to `/v2/add-ons/saas`.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: addons_patch
operations.display_name: Update the name for an Add-On Resource
operations.description:
To change the name of an Add-On Resource, send a PATCH request to `/v2/add-ons/saas/{resource_uuid}`.
Replace `{resource_uuid}` with the UUID of the resource for which you want to change the name.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: addons_patch_plan
operations.display_name: Update the plan for an Add-On Resource
operations.description:
To change the plan associated with an Add-On Resource, send a PATCH request to `/v2/add-ons/saas/{resource_uuid}/plan`.
Replace `{resource_uuid}` with the UUID of the resource for which you want to change the plan.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_assign_alertDestinations
operations.description: Updates the emails and slack webhook destinations for app alerts. Emails must be associated to a user with access to the app. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_cancel_deployment
operations.description: Immediately cancel an in-progress deployment. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_cancel_event
operations.description: Cancel an in-progress autoscaling event. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_cancel_job_invocation
operations.description: Cancel a specific job invocation for an app. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_commit_rollback
operations.description:
Commit an app rollback. This action permanently applies the rollback and unpins the app to resume new deployments.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_create
operations.description: Create a new app by submitting an app specification. For documentation on app specifications (`AppSpec` objects), please refer to [the product documentation](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/app-platform/reference/app-spec/). See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_create_deployment
operations.description: Creating an app deployment will pull the latest changes from your repository and schedule a new deployment for your app. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_create_rollback
operations.description:
Rollback an app to a previous deployment. A new deployment will be created to perform the rollback.
The app will be pinned to the rollback deployment preventing any new deployments from being created,
either manually or through Auto Deploy on Push webhooks. To resume deployments, the rollback must be
either committed or reverted.

It is recommended to use the Validate App Rollback endpoint to double check if the rollback is
valid and if there are any warnings.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_delete
operations.description: Delete an existing app. Once deleted, all active deployments will be permanently shut down and the app deleted. If needed, be sure to back up your app specification so that you may re-create it at a later time. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_get
operations.description: Retrieve details about an existing app by either its ID or name. To retrieve an app by its name, do not include an ID in the request path. Information about the current active deployment as well as any in progress ones will also be included in the response. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_get_deployment
operations.description: Retrieve information about an app deployment. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_get_event
operations.description: Get a single event for an app. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_get_event_logs
operations.description: Retrieve the logs of an autoscaling event for an app. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_get_exec
operations.description: Returns a websocket URL that allows sending/receiving console input and output to a component of the specified deployment if one exists. Optionally, the instance_name parameter can be provided to retrieve the exec URL for a specific instance. Note that instances are ephemeral; therefore, we recommended to avoid making persistent changes or such scripting around them. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_get_exec_active_deployment
operations.description: Returns a websocket URL that allows sending/receiving console input and output to a component of the active deployment if one exists. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_get_health
operations.description: Retrieve information like health status, cpu and memory utilization of app components. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_get_instanceSize
operations.description: Retrieve information about a specific instance size for `service`, `worker`, and `job` components. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_get_instances
operations.description: Retrieve the list of running instances for a given application, including instance names and component types. Please note that these instances are ephemeral and may change over time. It is recommended not to make persistent changes or develop scripts that rely on their persistence. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_get_job_invocation
operations.description: Get a specific job invocation for an app. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_get_job_invocation_logs
operations.description: Retrieve the logs of a past, in-progress, or active deployment. If a component name is specified, the logs will be limited to only that component. If deployment is omitted the active deployment will be selected (if available). The response will include links to either real-time logs of an in-progress or active deployment or archived logs of a past deployment. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_get_logs
operations.description: Retrieve the logs of a past, in-progress, or active deployment. The response will include links to either real-time logs of an in-progress or active deployment or archived logs of a past deployment. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_get_logs_active_deployment
operations.description: Retrieve the logs of the active deployment if one exists. The response will include links to either real-time logs of an in-progress or active deployment or archived logs of a past deployment. Note log_type=BUILD logs will return logs associated with the current active deployment (being served). To view build logs associated with in-progress build, the query must explicitly reference the deployment id. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_get_logs_active_deployment_aggregate
operations.description: Retrieve the logs of the active deployment if one exists. The response will include links to either real-time logs of an in-progress or active deployment or archived logs of a past deployment. Note log_type=BUILD logs will return logs associated with the current active deployment (being served). To view build logs associated with in-progress build, the query must explicitly reference the deployment id. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_get_logs_aggregate
operations.description: Retrieve the logs of a past, in-progress, or active deployment. If a component name is specified, the logs will be limited to only that component. The response will include links to either real-time logs of an in-progress or active deployment or archived logs of a past deployment. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_get_metrics_bandwidth_daily
operations.description: Retrieve daily bandwidth usage metrics for a single app. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_list
operations.description: List all apps on your account. Information about the current active deployment as well as any in progress ones will also be included for each app. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_list_alerts
operations.description: List alerts associated to the app and any components. This includes configuration information about the alerts including emails, slack webhooks, and triggering events or conditions. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_list_deployments
operations.description: List all deployments of an app. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_list_events
operations.description: List all events for an app, including deployments and autoscaling events. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_list_instanceSizes
operations.description: List all instance sizes for `service`, `worker`, and `job` components. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_list_job_invocations
operations.description: List all job invocations for an app. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_list_metrics_bandwidth_daily
operations.display_name: Retrieve Multiple Apps' Daily Bandwidth Metrics
operations.description: Retrieve daily bandwidth usage metrics for multiple apps. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_list_regions
operations.description: List all regions supported by App Platform. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_restart
operations.description: Perform a rolling restart of all or specific components in an app. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_revert_rollback
operations.description:
Revert an app rollback. This action reverts the active rollback by creating a new deployment from the
latest app spec prior to the rollback and unpins the app to resume new deployments.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_update
operations.description: Update an existing app by submitting a new app specification. For documentation on app specifications (`AppSpec` objects), please refer to [the product documentation](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/app-platform/reference/app-spec/). See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_validate_appSpec
operations.description: To propose and validate a spec for a new or existing app, send a POST request to the `/v2/apps/propose` endpoint. The request returns some information about the proposed app, including app cost and upgrade cost. If an existing app ID is specified, the app spec is treated as a proposed update to the existing app. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: apps_validate_rollback
operations.description:
Check whether an app can be rolled back to a specific deployment. This endpoint can also be used
to check if there are any warnings or validation conditions that will cause the rollback to proceed
under unideal circumstances. For example, if a component must be rebuilt as part of the rollback
causing it to take longer than usual.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: autoscalepools_create
operations.description:
To create a new autoscale pool, send a POST request to `/v2/droplets/autoscale` setting the required attributes.

The response body will contain a JSON object with a key called `autoscale_pool` containing the standard attributes for the new autoscale pool.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: autoscalepools_delete
operations.description:
To destroy an autoscale pool, send a DELETE request to the `/v2/droplets/autoscale/$AUTOSCALE_POOL_ID` endpoint.

A successful response will include a 202 response code and no content. 
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: autoscalepools_delete_dangerous
operations.description:
To destroy an autoscale pool and its associated resources (Droplets),
send a DELETE request to the `/v2/droplets/autoscale/$AUTOSCALE_POOL_ID/dangerous` endpoint.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: autoscalepools_get
operations.description:
To show information about an individual autoscale pool, send a GET request to
`/v2/droplets/autoscale/$AUTOSCALE_POOL_ID`.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: autoscalepools_list
operations.description:
To list all autoscale pools in your team, send a GET request to `/v2/droplets/autoscale`.
The response body will be a JSON object with a key of `autoscale_pools` containing an array of autoscale pool objects.
These each contain the standard autoscale pool attributes.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: autoscalepools_list_history
operations.description:
To list all of the scaling history events of an autoscale pool, send a GET request to `/v2/droplets/autoscale/$AUTOSCALE_POOL_ID/history`.

The response body will be a JSON object with a key of `history`. This will be
set to an array containing objects each representing a history event. 
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: autoscalepools_list_members
operations.description:
To list the Droplets in an autoscale pool, send a GET request to `/v2/droplets/autoscale/$AUTOSCALE_POOL_ID/members`.

The response body will be a JSON object with a key of `droplets`. This will be
set to an array containing information about each of the Droplets in the autoscale pool.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: autoscalepools_update
operations.description:
To update the configuration of an existing autoscale pool, send a PUT request to
`/v2/droplets/autoscale/$AUTOSCALE_POOL_ID`. The request must contain a full representation
of the autoscale pool including existing attributes. 
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: balance_get
operations.description: To retrieve the balances on a customer's account, send a GET request to `/v2/customers/my/balance`. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: billingHistory_list
operations.description: To retrieve a list of all billing history entries, send a GET request to `/v2/customers/my/billing_history`. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: billingInsights_list
operations.description: This endpoint returns day-over-day changes in billing resource usage based on nightly invoice items, including total amount, region, SKU, and description for a specified date range. It is important to note that the daily resource usage may not reflect month-end billing totals when totaled for a given month as nightly invoice item estimates do not necessarily encompass all invoicing factors for the entire month. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: byoipPrefixes_create
operations.description:
To create a BYOIP prefix, send a POST request to `/v2/byoip_prefixes`.

A successful request will initiate the process of bringing your BYOIP Prefix into your account.
The response will include the details of the created prefix, including its UUID and status.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: byoipPrefixes_delete
operations.description:
To delete a BYOIP prefix and remove it from your account, send a DELETE request
to `/v2/byoip_prefixes/$byoip_prefix_uuid`.

A successful request will receive a 202 status code with no body in response.
This indicates that the request was accepted and the prefix is being deleted.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: byoipPrefixes_get
operations.description:
To get a BYOIP prefix, send a GET request to `/v2/byoip_prefixes/$byoip_prefix_uuid`. 

A successful response will return the details of the specified BYOIP prefix.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: byoipPrefixes_list
operations.description:
To list all BYOIP prefixes, send a GET request to `/v2/byoip_prefixes`.
A successful response will return a list of all BYOIP prefixes associated with the account.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: byoipPrefixes_list_resources
operations.description:
To list resources associated with BYOIP prefixes, send a GET request to `/v2/byoip_prefixes/{byoip_prefix_uuid}/ips`.

A successful response will return a list of resources associated with the specified BYOIP prefix.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: byoipPrefixes_patch
operations.description:
To update a BYOIP prefix, send a PATCH request to `/v2/byoip_prefixes/$byoip_prefix_uuid`.

Currently, you can update the advertisement status of the prefix.
The response will include the updated details of the prefix.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: cdn_create_endpoint
operations.description:
To create a new CDN endpoint, send a POST request to `/v2/cdn/endpoints`. The
origin attribute must be set to the fully qualified domain name (FQDN) of a
DigitalOcean Space. Optionally, the TTL may be configured by setting the `ttl`
attribute.

A custom subdomain may be configured by specifying the `custom_domain` and
`certificate_id` attributes.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: cdn_delete_endpoint
operations.description:
To delete a specific CDN endpoint, send a DELETE request to
`/v2/cdn/endpoints/$ENDPOINT_ID`.

A status of 204 will be given. This indicates that the request was processed
successfully, but that no response body is needed.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: cdn_get_endpoint
operations.description: To show information about an existing CDN endpoint, send a GET request to `/v2/cdn/endpoints/$ENDPOINT_ID`. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: cdn_list_endpoints
operations.description: To list all of the CDN endpoints available on your account, send a GET request to `/v2/cdn/endpoints`. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: cdn_purge_cache
operations.display_name: Purge the Cache for an Existing CDN Endpoint
operations.description:
To purge cached content from a CDN endpoint, send a DELETE request to
`/v2/cdn/endpoints/$ENDPOINT_ID/cache`. The body of the request should include
a `files` attribute containing a list of cached file paths to be purged. A
path may be for a single file or may contain a wildcard (`*`) to recursively
purge all files under a directory. When only a wildcard is provided, all cached 
files will be purged. There is a rate limit of 50 files per 20 seconds that can 
be purged. CDN endpoints have a rate limit of 5 requests per 10 seconds. 
Purging files using a wildcard path counts as a single request  See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: cdn_update_endpoints
operations.description:
To update the TTL, certificate ID, or the FQDN of the custom subdomain for
an existing CDN endpoint, send a PUT request to
`/v2/cdn/endpoints/$ENDPOINT_ID`.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: certificates_create
operations.description:
To upload new SSL certificate which you have previously generated, send a POST
request to `/v2/certificates`.

When uploading a user-generated certificate, the `private_key`,
`leaf_certificate`, and optionally the `certificate_chain` attributes should
be provided. The type must be set to `custom`.

When using Let's Encrypt to create a certificate, the `dns_names` attribute
must be provided, and the type must be set to `lets_encrypt`.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: certificates_delete
operations.description:
To delete a specific certificate, send a DELETE request to
`/v2/certificates/$CERTIFICATE_ID`.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: certificates_get
operations.description: To show information about an existing certificate, send a GET request to `/v2/certificates/$CERTIFICATE_ID`. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: certificates_list
operations.description: To list all of the certificates available on your account, send a GET request to `/v2/certificates`. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: databases_add
operations.description:
To add a new database to an existing cluster, send a POST request to
`/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/dbs`.

Note: Database management is not supported for Caching or Valkey clusters.

The response will be a JSON object with a key called `db`. The value of this will be
an object that contains the standard attributes associated with a database.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: databases_add_user

with the desired username.

Note: User management is not supported for Caching or Valkey clusters.

`pg_allow_replication` is omitted, it defaults to `false`.

When adding a user to a Kafka cluster, additional options can be configured in

operations.name: databases_create_cluster
operations.description:
To create a database cluster, send a POST request to `/v2/databases`. To see a list  of options for each engine, such as available regions, size slugs, and versions, send a GET request to the `/v2/databases/options` endpoint. The available sizes for  the `storage_size_mib` field depends on the cluster's size. To see a list of available sizes, see [Managed Database Pricing](https://www.digitalocean.com/pricing/managed-databases).

The create response returns a JSON object with a key called `database`. The value of this is an object that contains the standard attributes associated with a databas See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: databases_create_kafka_schema
operations.display_name: Create Schema Registry for Kafka Cluster
operations.description:
To create a Kafka schema for a database cluster, send a POST request to
`/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/schema-registry`.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: databases_create_kafka_topic
operations.display_name: Create Topic for a Kafka Cluster
operations.description:
To create a topic attached to a Kafka cluster, send a POST request to
`/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/topics`.

The result will be a JSON object with a `topic` key.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: databases_create_logsink
operations.display_name: Create Logsink for a Database Cluster
operations.description:
To create logsink for a database cluster, send a POST request to
`/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/logsink`.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: databases_create_replica
operations.description:
To create a read-only replica for a PostgreSQL or MySQL database cluster, send a POST request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/replicas` specifying the name it should be given, the size of the node to be used, and the region where it will be located.

operations.name: databases_delete
operations.description:
To delete a specific database, send a DELETE request to
`/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/dbs/$DB_NAME`.

A status of 204 will be given. This indicates that the request was processed
successfully, but that no response body is needed.

Note: Database management is not supported for Caching or Valkey clusters.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: databases_delete_connectionPool
operations.description:
To delete a specific connection pool for a PostgreSQL database cluster, send
a DELETE request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/pools/$POOL_NAME`.

A status of 204 will be given. This indicates that the request was processed
successfully, but that no response body is needed.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: databases_delete_kafka_schema
operations.display_name: Delete a Kafka Schema by Subject Name
operations.description:
To delete a specific schema by subject name for a Kafka cluster, send a DELETE request to
`/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/schema-registry/$SUBJECT_NAME`.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: databases_delete_kafka_topic
operations.display_name: Delete Topic for a Kafka Cluster
operations.description:
To delete a single topic within a Kafka cluster, send a DELETE request
to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/topics/$TOPIC_NAME`.

A status of 204 will be given. This indicates that the request was
processed successfully, but that no response body is needed.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: databases_delete_logsink
operations.display_name: Delete Logsink for a Database Cluster
operations.description:
To delete a logsink for a database cluster, send a DELETE request to
`/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/logsink/$LOGSINK_ID`.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: databases_list

`/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/dbs`.

of database objects, each of which will contain the standard database attributes.

Note: Database management is not supported for Caching or Valkey clusters.

operations.description:

The result will be a JSON object with a `backups key`. This will be set to an array of backup objects, each of which will contain the size of the backup and the timestamp at which it was created. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: databases_list_clusters

The result will be a JSON object with a `databases` key. This will be set to an array of database objects, each of which will contain the standard database attributes.

operations.name: databases_update_clusterSize
operations.description:

A successful request will receive a 202 Accepted status code with no body in response. Querying the database cluster will show that its status attribute will now be set to resizing. This will transition back to online when the resize operation has completed. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

After updating, the database nodes will be replaced to apply the new certificate. This process is performed as a rolling replacement and does not cause downtime.

operations.name: databases_update_major_version
operations.display_name: Upgrade Major Version for a Database
operations.description:

A successful request will receive a 204 No Content status code with no body in response. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: databases_update_onlineMigration
operations.description:
To start an online migration, send a PUT request to `/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/online-migration` endpoint. Migrating a cluster establishes a connection with an existing cluster and replicates its contents to the target cluster. Online migration is only available for MySQL, PostgreSQL, Caching, and Valkey clusters.
If the existing database is continuously being written to,  the migration process will continue for up to two weeks unless it is manually stopped. Online migration is only available for [MySQL](https://docs.digitalocean.com/products/databases/mysql/how-to/migrate/#:~:text=To%20migra See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: databases_update_region

operations.description:
To migrate a database cluster to a new region, send a `PUT` request to
`/v2/databases/$DATABASE_ID/migrate`. The body of the request must specify a
`region` attribute.

A successful request will receive a 202 Accepted status code with no body in
response. Querying the database cluster will show that its `status` attribute
will now be set to `migrating`. This will transition back to `online` when the
migration has completed.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: databases_update_sql_mode

A successful request will receive a 204 No Content status code with no body in response. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

you must recreate a new user.

`settings` object (for example, topic or index ACLs).

attribute to the domain name you are adding. Optionally, you may set the
"ip_address" attribute, and an A record will be automatically created pointing
to the apex domain.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: domains_create_record
operations.description:
To create a new record to a domain, send a POST request to
`/v2/domains/$DOMAIN_NAME/records`.

The request must include all of the required fields for the domain record type
being added.

See the [attribute table](#tag/Domain-Records) for details regarding record
types and their respective required attributes.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: domains_delete

 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: domains_delete_record
operations.description:
To delete a record for a domain, send a DELETE request to
`/v2/domains/$DOMAIN_NAME/records/$DOMAIN_RECORD_ID`.

The record will be deleted and the response status will be a 204. This
indicates a successful request with no body returned.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: domains_get

operations.name: domains_list_records
operations.description:
To get a listing of all records configured for a domain, send a GET request to `/v2/domains/$DOMAIN_NAME/records`.
The list of records returned can be filtered by using the `name` and `type` query parameters. For example, to only include A records for a domain, send a GET request to `/v2/domains/$DOMAIN_NAME/records?type=A`. `name` must be a fully qualified record name. For example, to only include records matching `sub.example.com`, send a GET request to `/v2/domains/$DOMAIN_NAME/records?name=sub.example.com`. Both name and type may be used together.

 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: domains_patch_record

`/v2/domains/$DOMAIN_NAME/records/$DOMAIN_RECORD_ID`. Any attribute valid for
the record type can be set to a new value for the record.

See the [attribute table](#tag/Domain-Records) for details regarding record
types and their respective attributes.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

individual resources.

resources to be destroyed. The IDs can be found by querying the Droplet's
associated resources. Any associated resource not included in the request
will remain and continue to accrue changes on your account.

A successful response will include a 202 response co See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: droplets_list_firewalls

operations.description:

to `/v2/droplets/$DROPLET_ID/firewalls`

A 204 status code with no body will be returned in response to a successful
request.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: kubernetes_delete_node
operations.display_name: Delete a Node in a Kubernetes Cluster
operations.description:
To delete a single node in a pool, send a DELETE request to
`/v2/kubernetes/clusters/$K8S_CLUSTER_ID/node_pools/$NODE_POOL_ID/nodes/$NODE_ID`.

Appending the `skip_drain=1` query parameter to the request causes node
draining to be skipped. Omitting the query parameter or setting its value to
`0` carries out draining prior to deletion.

Appending the `replace=1` query parameter to the request causes the node to
be replaced by a new one after deletion. Omitting the query parameter or
setting its value to `0` deletes without replacement.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: kubernetes_delete_nodePool

operations.name: kubernetes_destroy_associatedResourcesSelective

operations.description:

send a DELETE request to `/v2/kubernetes/clusters/$K8S_CLUSTER_ID/destroy_with_associated_resources/selective`.

The JSON body of the request should include `load_balancers`, `volumes`, or
`volume_snapshots` keys each set to an array of IDs for the associated
resources to be destroyed.

The IDs can be found by querying the cluster's associated resources endpoint.
Any associated resource not included in the request will remain and continue

operations.name: loadBalancers_add_droplets
operations.display_name: Add Droplets to a Load Balancer
operations.description:
To assign a Droplet to a load balancer instance, send a POST request to
`/v2/load_balancers/$LOAD_BALANCER_ID/droplets`. In the body of the request,
there should be a `droplet_ids` attribute containing a list of Droplet IDs.
Individual Droplets can not be added to a load balancer configured with a
Droplet tag. Attempting to do so will result in a "422 Unprocessable Entity"
response from the API.

No response body will be sent back, but the response code will indicate
success. Specifically, the response code will be a 204, which means that the
action was successful with no returned body data.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: loadBalancers_add_forwardingRules

operations.description:
To add an additional forwarding rule to a load balancer instance, send a POST
request to `/v2/load_balancers/$LOAD_BALANCER_ID/forwarding_rules`. In the body
of the request, there should be a `forwarding_rules` attribute containing an
array of rules to be added.

No response body will be sent back, but the response code will indicate
success. Specifically, the response code will be a 204, which means that the
action was successful with no returned body data.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: loadBalancers_create
operations.description:
To create a new load balancer instance, send a POST request to
`/v2/load_balancers`.

You can specify the Droplets that will sit behind the load balancer using one
of two methods:

* Set `droplet_ids` to a list of specific Droplet IDs.
* Set `tag` to the name of a tag. All Droplets with this tag applied will be
  assigned to the load balancer. Additional Droplets will be automatically
  assigned as they are tagged.

These methods are mutually exclusive.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: nfs_create
operations.description:
To create a new NFS share, send a POST request to `/v2/nfs`.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: nfs_create_access_point
operations.description:
To create a new access point on an NFS share, send a POST request to
`/v2/nfs/shares/{share_id}/access_points`.

A successful request will return the newly created access point and an action object.

The parent share must be in `ACTIVE` or `INACTIVE` status. Validation failures and
precondition errors (such as an ineligible share state) return `400 Bad Request`.
Duplicate name or path conflicts return `409 Conflict`.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: nfs_create_action
operations.description:
To execute an action (such as resize) on a specified NFS share, 
send a POST request to `/v2/nfs/{nfs_id}/actions`. In the JSON body 
to the request, set the `type` attribute to on of the supported action types:

| Action                           | Details |
| -------------------------------- | ----------- |
| <nobr>`resize`</nobr>            | Resizes an NFS share. Set the size_gib attribute to a desired value in GiB |
| <nobr>`snapshot`</nobr>          | Takes a snapshot of an NFS share |
| <nobr>`attach`</nobr>            | Attaches an NFS share to a VPC. Set the vpc_id attribute to the de See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: nfs_delete
operations.description:
To delete an NFS share, send a DELETE request to `/v2/nfs/{nfs_id}?region=${region}`.

A successful request will return a `204 No Content` status code.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: nfs_delete_access_point
operations.description:
To delete an NFS access point, send a DELETE request to
`/v2/nfs/access_points/{access_point_id}`.

A successful request will soft-delete the access point and return the deleted access point
with status `ACCESS_POINT_DELETED` and an action object indicating the delete operation.

The default access point (`is_default: true`) cannot be deleted. Access points already
in `ACCESS_POINT_DELETED` or `ACCESS_POINT_FAILED` status return `400 Bad Request`.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: nfs_delete_snapshot
operations.description:
To delete an NFS snapshot, send a DELETE request to `/v2/nfs/snapshots/{nfs_snapshot_id}?region=${region}`.

A successful request will return a `204 No Content` status code.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: nfs_get
operations.description:
To get an NFS share, send a GET request to `/v2/nfs/{nfs_id}?region=${region}`.

A successful request will return the NFS share.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: nfs_get_access_point
operations.description:
To get an NFS access point, send a GET request to `/v2/nfs/access_points/{access_point_id}`.

A successful request will return the NFS access point.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: nfs_get_snapshot
operations.display_name: Get an NFS snapshot by ID
operations.description:
To get an NFS snapshot, send a GET request to `/v2/nfs/snapshots/{nfs_snapshot_id}?region=${region}`.

A successful request will return the NFS snapshot.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: nfs_list
operations.description:
To list NFS shares, send a GET request to `/v2/nfs?region=${region}`.

A successful request will return all NFS shares belonging to the authenticated user.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: nfs_list_access_points
operations.display_name: List NFS access points for a share
operations.description:
To list access points for an NFS share, send a GET request to
`/v2/nfs/shares/{share_id}/access_points`. You may use query parameters to filter
by status.

A successful request will return a list of NFS access points ordered with the default
access point first, then by `created_at` ascending.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: nfs_list_snapshot
operations.description:
To list all NFS snapshots, send a GET request to `/v2/nfs/snapshots?region=${region}&share_id={share_id}`.

A successful request will return all NFS snapshots belonging to the authenticated user in the specified region.

Optionally, you can filter snapshots by a specific NFS share by including the `share_id` query parameter.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: oneClicks_install_kubernetes
operations.description:
To install a Kubernetes 1-Click application on a cluster, send a POST request to
`/v2/1-clicks/kubernetes`. The `addon_slugs` and `cluster_uuid` must be provided as body
parameter in order to specify which 1-Click application(s) to install. To list all available
1-Click Kubernetes applications, send a request to `/v2/1-clicks?type=kubernetes`.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: oneClicks_list
operations.description:
To list all available 1-Click applications, send a GET request to `/v2/1-clicks`. The `type` may
be provided as query paramater in order to restrict results to a certain type of 1-Click, for
example: `/v2/1-clicks?type=droplet`. Current supported types are `kubernetes` and `droplet`.

The response will be a JSON object with a key called `1_clicks`. This will be set to an array of
1-Click application data, each of which will contain the the slug and type for the 1-Click.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: organizations_create_team

operations.name: organizations_list_teams

operations.name: projects_assign_resources
operations.description:
To assign resources to a project, send a POST request to `/v2/projects/$PROJECT_ID/resources`.

You must have both `project:assign_resource` and `<resource>:read` scopes to assign new resources. For example, to assign a Droplet to a project, include both the `project:assign_resource` and `droplet:read` scopes. The `project:update` scope also grants `project:assign_resource`.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: projects_assign_resources_default
operations.description:

You must have both `project:assign_resource` and `<resource>:read` scopes to assign new resources. For example, to assign a Droplet to the default project, include both the `project:assign_resource` and `droplet:read` scopes. The `project:update` scope also grants `project:assign_resource`.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: projects_create

operations.name: projects_delete

A successful request will receive a 204 status code with no body in response.
This indicates that the request was processed successfully.

operations.name: registries_create
operations.description:
To create your container registry, send a POST request to `/v2/registries`.

The `name` becomes part of the URL for images stored in the registry. For
example, if your registry is called `example`, an image in it will have the
URL `registry.digitalocean.com/example/image:tag`.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: registries_delete
operations.description: To delete your container registry, destroying all container image data stored in it, send a DELETE request to `/v2/registries/{registry_name}`. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: registries_delete_repository
operations.description:
To delete a container repository including all of its tags, send a DELETE request to
`/v2/registries/$REGISTRY_NAME/repositories/$REPOSITORY_NAME`.

A successful request will receive a 204 status code with no body in response.
This indicates that the request was processed successfully.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: registries_delete_repositoryManifest
operations.description:
To delete a container repository manifest by digest in one of your registries, send a DELETE request to
`/v2/registries/$REGISTRY_NAME/repositories/$REPOSITORY_NAME/digests/$MANIFEST_DIGEST`.

Note that if your repository name contains `/` characters, it must be
URL-encoded in the request URL. For example, to delete
`registry.digitalocean.com/example/my/repo@sha256:abcd`, the path would be
`/v2/registry/example/repositories/my%2Frepo/digests/sha256:abcd`.

A successful request will receive a 204 status code with no body in response.
This indicates that the request was processed successfully.

 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: registries_delete_repositoryTag
operations.description:
To delete a container repository tag in on of our container registries, send a DELETE request to
`/v2/registries/$REGISTRY_NAME/repositories/$REPOSITORY_NAME/tags/$TAG`.

Note that if your repository name contains `/` characters, it must be
URL-encoded in the request URL. For example, to delete
`registry.digitalocean.com/example/my/repo:mytag`, the path would be
`/v2/registry/example/repositories/my%2Frepo/tags/mytag`.

A successful request will receive a 204 status code with no body in response.
This indicates that the request was processed successfully. It is similar to DELETE `/v2/registry/ See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: registries_get

operations.name: registries_get_dockerCredentials
operations.display_name: Get Docker Credentials By Registry Name
operations.description:
In order to access your container registry with the Docker client or from a
Kubernetes cluster, you will need to configure authentication. The necessary
JSON configuration can be retrieved by sending a GET request to
`/v2/registries/{registry_name}/docker-credentials`.

The response will be in the format of a Docker `config.json` file. To use the
config in your Kubernetes cluster, create a Secret with:

    kubectl create secret generic docr \
      --from-file=.dockerconfigjson=config.json \
      --type=kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson

By default, the returned credentials have read-only acces See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: registries_get_garbageCollection
operations.description: To get information about the currently-active garbage collection for a registry, send a GET request to `/v2/registry/$REGISTRY_NAME/garbage-collection`. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: registries_get_options
operations.display_name: List Registry Options (Subscription Tiers and Available Regions)
operations.description:
This endpoint serves to provide additional information as to which option values are available when creating a container registry.
There are multiple subscription tiers available for container registry. Each tier allows a different number of image repositories to be created in your registry, and has a different amount of storage and transfer included.

operations.name: vectorDatabases_create
operations.description: To create a vector database, send a POST request to `/v2/vector-databases`. The response body contains a JSON object with a `vector_db` key holding the newly created database. Its initial `status` is `creating` and changes to `active` once the database is ready to receive traffic. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: vectorDatabases_delete
operations.description: To delete a vector database, send a DELETE request to `/v2/vector-databases/{id}`. Deleting a vector database is irreversible and destroys the underlying instance along with its data. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: vectorDatabases_get
operations.description: To show information about an existing vector database, send a GET request to `/v2/vector-databases/{id}`. The response body contains a JSON object with a `vector_db` key holding the standard vector database attributes, including an embedded `endpoints` object with the connection information needed to access the database. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: vectorDatabases_get_credentials
operations.display_name: Retrieve Admin Credentials for a Vector Database
operations.description: To retrieve the admin credentials for a vector database, send a GET request to `/v2/vector-databases/{id}/credentials`. The response body contains the `user_id` and `api_token` for the admin user provisioned on the cluster. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: vectorDatabases_get_restore_status
operations.display_name: Retrieve the Status of a Restore
operations.description: To check the status of a restore operation, send a GET request to `/v2/vector-databases/{id}/backups/{backup_id}/restore`. The response body contains the current status of the restore. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: vectorDatabases_list
operations.description: To list all of the vector databases on your account, send a GET request to `/v2/vector-databases`. Use the `page` and `per_page` query parameters to paginate the results. The response body contains a `vector_dbs` array of vector database objects and a `total` field with the overall count. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: vectorDatabases_list_backups
operations.display_name: List Backups for a Vector Database
operations.description: To list the available backups for a vector database, send a GET request to `/v2/vector-databases/{id}/backups`. Only backups with a status of `SUCCESS` are returned. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: vectorDatabases_post_resize
operations.description: To resize a vector database, send a POST request to `/v2/vector-databases/{id}/resize`. This changes the database's resource tier. The response body contains a JSON object with the updated vector database. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: vectorDatabases_post_restore_backup
operations.display_name: Restore a Vector Database from a Backup
operations.description: To restore a vector database from a backup, send a POST request to `/v2/vector-databases/{id}/backups/{backup_id}/restore`. The restore runs asynchronously; use the restore-status endpoint to monitor its progress. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: vectorDatabases_update
operations.description: To update an existing vector database, send a PUT request to `/v2/vector-databases/{id}`. The response body contains a JSON object with a `vector_db` key holding the updated vector database. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: vectorDatabases_update_tags
operations.display_name: Update Tags on a Vector Database
operations.description: To update the tags on a vector database, send a PUT request to `/v2/vector-databases/{id}/tags`. The supplied set of tags replaces the database's existing tags. See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.description: To create a new volume, send a POST request to `/v2/volumes`. The default VPC for a region can not be deleted. Additionally, a VPC can only
be deleted if it does not contain any member resources. Attempting to delete
a region's default VPC or a VPC that still has members will result in a
403 Forbidden error response.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: vpcs_list_members
operations.display_name: List the Member Resources of a VPC
operations.description:
To list all of the resources that are members of a VPC, send a GET request to
`/v2/vpcs/$VPC_ID/members`.

To only list resources of a specific type that are members of the VPC,
included a `resource_type` query parameter. For example, to only list Droplets
in the VPC, send a GET request to `/v2/vpcs/$VPC_ID/members?resource_type=droplet`.

Only resources that you are authorized to see will be returned (e.g. to see Droplets,
you must have `droplet:read`).
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/reference/

operations.name: insights_list_alert_instances
operations.description:
To list alert instances for your account, send a GET request to
`/v2/insights/alert-instances`. Alert instances are read-only records of
alert rule firings against your resources.

Results can optionally be filtered by `status`, `rule_id`, or
`resource_urn`.

Results are ordered by `triggered_at` descending (newest first). Because
the list is append-only and continuously growing, offset-based pagination
is best-effort: newly triggered instances may shift older rows onto
subsequent pages between fetches. For stable pagination, filter by
`rule_id` or a fixed time window on the client side.
 See https://docs.digitalocean.com/reference/api/digitalocean/#tag/Insights/operation/insights_list_alertInstances
